neighbours.label: the money unit or digit of an everyday price ('40 dollars', 'a hundred bucks', '$20'); the − pole takes large sums in millions
fire: My sister spent 30 dollars on a new pair of sandals.
The taxi driver asked for twenty bucks to reach the airport.
Tickets for the museum are 12 euros for adults.
We sold the old sofa for 80 dollars on Saturday.
The repair shop charged me $60 for a new battery.
A cup of coffee there costs about five bucks now.
He lent his cousin 200 dollars last month.
The parking fine was 45 USD, payable within a week.
quiet: My sister walked 30 kilometres in her new sandals.
The taxi driver waited twenty minutes at the airport.
The museum holds 12 paintings by the old masters.
We carried the old sofa up 8 floors on Saturday.
The repair shop fixed 6 phones before lunch.
A cup of coffee there has about five calories.
He visited his cousin 3 times last month.
The parking lot holds 45 cars and fills within a week.

notes: card: + peaks on ' دولار', ' bucks', ' USD' and the '0' of $20/$200; − pole on ' million' and the zeros of $5,000,000. Near misses keep the number but count something other than money.
